The Solasaurus, or "lonely dinosaur," first discovered in 1892 by English nobleman Sir George Olduvai while exploring what is now modern-day Tanganyika, was long thought to be a solitary, non-herd animal which led an isolated lifestyle for unknown reasons. Analysis of a rare-but-well-preserved fossilized specimen, found in south China, which contained considerable esophageal soft tissue has allowed scientists to reconstruct a vocal apparatus which, though somewhat speculative, shows that construction of the Solasaurus' vocal chords and resonant cavities were best suited for pejorative grunts sounding similar to "fahkew", leading to updated conclusion that the Solasaurus was most likely perceived by other species as just a jackass and overtly shunned. Some researchers have informally begun referring to the Solasaurus as "Tourettesaurus Rex".
